findings.message: At 100 bp per bin, 21.2% of called bins are heterozygous (K), which implies 2.39 heterozygous sites per kb and about 11.4% of K bins holding two or more of them (more if heterozygosity varies along the genome). PSMC only sees whether a bin holds one, so the oldest part of the curve loses resolution.
findings.recommendation: Re-bin the per-site data at 43 bp per bin or less, the largest size that keeps the share below 5.0% at this heterozygosity: `--bin-size 43` for VCF and multihetsep input, or `fq2psmcfa -s 43` for a psmcfa file, which psmc-rs then reads with `--bin-size 43` so that the results are scaled with the same bin size.

findings.message: 97.0% of bins lie in 1,219 sequences shorter than the bootstrap trunk (500,000 bins), which the bootstrap can only resample whole.
findings.recommendation: For the bootstrap, a trunk of at most 52,847 bins keeps at least 80.0% of bins in sequences of one trunk or more (--bootstrap-block-size).

findings.message: This input records which bins are called (at least 10% of their 100 bases callable, fq2psmcfa's rule) but not how many of their bases are, as psmcfa does, so the fit treats every called bin as 100 bases, as C psmc does. 3.8% of bins are missing (N), and 191,470 called bins (1.0% of them) border those runs: they hold fewer than 100 callable bases unless a run starts or ends at a bin boundary. If missing data are also scattered in runs shorter than a bin, most called bins do, which this input cannot show. Partly callable bins show fewer heterozygous sites, which biases theta, the times and Ne low by about their missing share.
findings.recommendation: To measure it, run `psmc-rs qc` on the data the psmcfa was made from: a VCF with its callable mask (--vcf-mask) or an all-sites VCF from `bcftools call -c`. It reports the share of callable bases of the called bins, and a fit of that VCF weighs each bin by its callable bases (--bin-callable auto), which removes the bias.

findings.message: 17 of 207 sequences with at least 1.00 Mb in called bins have a heterozygosity far from their median of 2.43 per kb (more than 5 MADs of log theta and 1.5-fold): ML685846.1 (0.0049x), ML688392.1 (0.0063x), ML688485.1 (0.0080x), ML688283.1 (0.010x), ML686217.1 (0.015x), ML688537.1 (0.019x), ML688284.1 (0.020x), ML688386.1 (0.022x), ML688390.1 (0.022x), ML686214.1 (0.051x) and 7 more.
findings.recommendation: High heterozygosity can come from contamination, collapsed duplications or copy-number variants, or reference errors; low heterozygosity from sex-linked scaffolds (near zero when hemizygous), runs of homozygosity (inbreeding, a real signal), deletions or an over-strict mask. Check depth, mapping quality, the mask and the chromosome assignment of these sequences, and exclude any that are artefacts or hemizygous.
